# Discrete Computational Models

In the case that your domain has finite discrete values, any function on that domain can be represented by polynomials. Since there are a finite number of inputs, each polynomial may be interpolated to agree with the function of a finite number of points.

A finite domain may be encoded by integers modulo something. We explore modular representation by roots of unity and $k$-bit binary.

We also discuss uses such as modular arithmetic, the sign function, and sorting, and consider the computational costs and numerical accuracy of these methods.
